Based on the screenshot and the report, the autoloader isn’t aware of “apex” – there is no entry for it in either the `lang_dependencies` map or the `lang_aliases` map.  As a result, when you mark a code block `data-language="apex"` Prism sees “apex” but doesn’t know how (or where) to load it.

The simplest solution is to teach the autoloader to treat “apex” exactly like Java:

  • In `lang_dependencies`, make Apex depend on the same prerequisites as Java (i.e. the “clike” core).  
  • In `lang_aliases`, alias “apex” to “java” so that it actually uses the Java grammar once it’s loaded.

Here are two small SEARCH/REPLACE patches for `plugins/autoloader/prism-autoloader.js`:

```javascript
### plugins/autoloader/prism-autoloader.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        "java": "clike",
        "javadoc": [
            "markup",
            "java",
            "javadoclike"
        ],
=======
        "java": "clike",
        "apex": "clike",
        "javadoc": [
            "markup",
            "java",
            "javadoclike"
        ],
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

```javascript
### plugins/autoloader/prism-autoloader.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    var lang_aliases = /*aliases_placeholder[*/{
        "html": "markup",
        "xml": "markup",
        "svg": "markup",
=======
    var lang_aliases = /*aliases_placeholder[*/{
        "html": "markup",
        "xml": "markup",
        "svg": "markup",
        "apex": "java",
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With those two additions:

 1. When you request `data-language="apex"`, the autoloader will first pull in `prism-clike.min.js` (because Apex is a C-style language),  
 2. Then it will pull in `prism-java.min.js` (because we map Apex → Java),  
 3. Finally your block stays tagged as “apex” so Prism will highlight it using the Java grammar under the hood.
